narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your current job. This slightly elevated risk is the main reason your promotion request was denied, as the organization aims to invest in employees more likely to stay long-term.

Three key factors shaped this outlook, with the strongest being that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. Most employees predicted to stay (77%) report no such external offers, so this availability appears to make leaving more realistic for you and pushes the prediction toward departure.

Next, your 6-10 years in your current role works in your favor. This tenure is longer than what most stayers have, signaling loyalty and stability that pulls the prediction back toward staying. Similarly, your overall 11+ years of professional experience also leans toward retention. While only 15% of predicted stayers have this much experience, the model sees it as a sign of commitment rather than a reason to move on.

Taken together, the external opportunities slightly outweigh your demonstrated loyalty, tipping the balance just over 50%. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You might explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer advancement paths, or addressing any unspoken concerns could strengthen your connection to the company and reduce the likelihood of leaving.
